title: Data pipeline for managing field experiments
author: Liu, Cichota, et al.

steps.title: Set up the R environment
steps.instruction: Prepare the R development environment to ensure reproducibility and secure access to data sources.

substeps.instruction: Use the renv package to create a renv.lock file to record package dependencies and version numbers.
Create an environment file in the user's private directory containing credentials for Windows New Technology LAN Manager (NTLM) protected shared servers and PostgreSQL database access.

steps.title: Implement the data pipeline functions
steps.instruction: Develop a set of 15 R functions stored in a 'functions.R' script, managed by the targets package, to handle data orchestration.

substeps.instruction: Create data source connection functions: one Excel adaptor for SharePoint server access and one for PostgreSQL database connection/upload.
Create a meteorological data retrieval function using the clifro package to automate Rain and PET data retrieval from the NIWA National Climate Database via API.
Create canopy data functions to standardize and interpolate fortnightly NDVI measurements to daily values, assuming linear development between emergence and closure (closure defined as NDVI = 0.75).

Create water balance calculation functions (8 functions total), including a specific function to estimate field capacity based on winter fallow period moisture and a core function implementing water balance equations.
Create utility functions for modifying time variables and performing lag time calculations.

steps.title: Deploy the visualization server
steps.instruction: Deploy Grafana as a service to visualize time-series data interactively.

substeps.instruction: Use a YAML file and the docker-compose command on a Linux server to build the Grafana Docker container (using the -d flag for background operation).
Access the Grafana interface via the Linux server URL (port 3000) or localhost (http://www.localhost:3000/).
Define the PostgreSQL database as the data source within Grafana.
Assemble dashboard widgets using the drag-and-drop interface.

steps.title: Execute the data pipeline
steps.instruction: Run the pipeline to process manual entries and update the visualization dashboard.

substeps.instruction: Manually upload soil moisture content (SWC), irrigation application rate, and NDVI data to Microsoft Excel spreadsheets on the SharePoint server.
Run the R executable program on the laboratory computer to trigger the targets data pipeline.

The pipeline will import Excel data, query NIWA weather data, apply the 13 transformation functions (including water balance and NDVI interpolation), and upload the summarized data to the PostgreSQL database.
Verify the results via the Grafana dashboard to make informed management decisions (e.g., irrigation or leachate sampling).
